A/R and A/P Report Sorting: the buttons of the "Switch location?" dialog

When the user clicks an invoice from another location they work at, a "Switch location?" dialog opens on the report. The design draws two buttons, "Cancel" on the left and "Switch Location" (capital L) on the right, plus a close "×" at the top right. The spec says the buttons are "Switch location" (small l) and "Cancel". Which is right?
(a) As the design: "Cancel", then "Switch Location" with a capital L, and the "×" closes the dialog like "Cancel".
(b) As the spec: "Switch location" with a small l (please also say the order of the buttons and whether there is a "×").
(c) Something else (please say).

The spec says: title "Switch location?" ... buttons "Switch location" and "Cancel", and calls it "the existing location-switch prompt". The design's picture of the dialog, and its caption "Switch Location opens it there.", show the capital L, the button order and the "×".

A/R and A/P Report Sorting: the search box in the Vendor filter

On the A/P reports, the Vendor filter's menu has a search box at the top. The design shows its hint text as "Search vendor"; the spec writes "Search vendors". Which is right?
(a) "Search vendors", as the spec says.
(b) "Search vendor", as the design shows.
(c) Whatever Inventory Value's Vendor filter shows today (the spec says the filter is exactly that one).
The spec says the Vendor filter is "exactly as Inventory Value's Vendor filter (truck icon, "Search vendors")". The design's picture of the open Vendor menu shows "Search vendor".
PRD v5 S5-R13; the design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), page 7 "The native Vendor menu"; Jira SV-11535 (Story 5)
A/R and A/P Report Sorting: the Totals row when no location is ticked

When the user clears the Location filter ("Location: No locations"), the report shows the empty state "No record matches these filters". The design also draws a Totals row reading $0.00 above the empty state; the spec says there are no totals. Which is right?
(a) No Totals row, as the spec says.
(b) A Totals row of $0.00, as the design shows.
(c) Something else (please say).

The spec says: "the native empty state (S8-R5) with "Clear all filters", no totals and no Location column". The design's picture "Cleared: No locations" shows "Totals $0.00 $0.00" under the column headings.
PRD v5 S5-R6a; the design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), page 4 "Cleared: No locations"; Jira SV-11535 (Story 5)
A/R and A/P Report Sorting: order of same-day invoices inside a customer on A/R Collection

On A/R Collection the invoices inside each customer are listed oldest date first. When several invoices have the same date, the spec says they are put in invoice number order. In the design's picture, five invoices of one customer all dated Aug 27, 2026 are not in number order (S3-14690, S3-14693, S3-15660, S3-14691, S3-14692). Which is right?
(a) Same-day invoices in number order, as the spec says (the picture is out of date).
(b) Same-day invoices in the order of the time they were invoiced that day, as the picture suggests.
(c) Something else (please say).

The spec says: "inside each group, rows open oldest date first, ties by document number". The design's picture "The customer row stays pinned" shows the five Aug 27, 2026 invoices out of number order. On A/R Detail the design's pictures do show ties in number order.
PRD v5 S1-R6, S2-R4; the design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), page 3 "The customer row stays pinned"; Jira SV-11531 (Story 1)
A/R and A/P Report Sorting: how links look (bold or regular)

On the six reports, invoice and bill numbers (and customer and vendor names on the Summaries) are blue links. The spec says links are "semi-bold"; in every design picture the links are blue but at the same weight as the plain text beside them. Which is right?
(a) Semi-bold, as the spec says.
(b) Regular weight, as the design shows.
(c) Exactly as Work In Progress's links look today (please say which that is).

The spec says: "Links use the native report link style (the same blue as Work In Progress, semi-bold, no underline, underlined only on keyboard focus)". The design's pictures (for example "Links only where they can open" and "A/R Aging Summary opens A to Z") show the links at regular weight.
